findings.label: Client-supplied HWID accepted at activation
findings.summary: /api/license/activate reads hwid from the request body and stores it directly. Any client can pass an arbitrary string, registering unlimited fake devices or spoofing another user's HWID.
findings.action: Remove hwid from the accepted body fields in the activate route. Determine the HWID server-side (or via a trusted client binary) rather than accepting it as an untrusted parameter.

findings.label: Server HWID used for license status — always mismatches in deployed environment
findings.summary: license_status_route and /api/status both call lic.get_hwid(), which fingerprints the server process's own machine. In any cloud/multi-user deployment, this will never match activations stored against user desktop HWIDs, returning active: False for all users.
findings.action: Decide the deployment model. If this is a web service, HWID binding must move to a client binary (Electron/desktop app) and the server must accept and attest the HWID from that binary. If it is a single-machine local app, document that constraint and remove the web UI activation path.

findings.label: Lock overlay is UI-only — no server enforcement
findings.summary: checkLicense() and .lock-overlay are client-side JavaScript only. No server middleware or route handler checks license.active before serving AI, rendering, or upload requests. Any authenticated user can call the API directly.
findings.action: Add a license check to the Gate middleware or to individual protected route handlers (upload, AI endpoints) that rejects requests when license_status returns active: False.

findings.label: admin_revoke_device has no ownership check on act_id
findings.summary: POST /api/admin/keys/{key}/devices/{act_id}/revoke passes act_id directly to admin_revoke_device(act_id), which updates any activation record matching that integer ID regardless of which key it belongs to.
findings.action: In admin_revoke_device, add a WHERE key = key condition alongside WHERE id = act_id so the update is scoped to the correct key.

findings.label: license_status write-amplification on every status poll
findings.summary: Every 15-second /api/status poll per authenticated user triggers a JOIN query plus an UPDATE last_seen write. At scale this produces significant unnecessary write load.
findings.action: Cache the license status result in memory (keyed by user_id) with a 60-second TTL, or update last_seen only when more than N minutes have passed since the previous update.
